Figure 3: RIG-I-only vs STAT-only signatures in nasal swabs of SARS-CoV-2 patients (scRNA-Seq)

Carlos Ramirez

2026-10-27 17:05:22

This markdown reproduces the panels of Figure 3. We project the RIG-I-only and STAT-only (IFN-only) signatures, derived from the A549 bulk model in Figure 1, onto the single-cell RNA-Seq data of nasal swabs from SARS-CoV-2 positive and negative children and adults published by Loske et al. 2021, Nat. Biotechnol.. Every cell is scored with both signatures (Seurat AddModuleScore), and cells are classified into two quadrants of the RIG-I-only vs STAT-only score plane using thresholds derived from SARS-CoV-2 negative donors (99.959 % quantile of the RIG-I-only score and 99.99 % quantile of the STAT-only score of all cells of SARS-CoV-2 negative donors):

  • Quadrant I: RIG-I-only score above threshold and STAT-only score below threshold (cells with direct RIG-I activity but no IFN-receptor signalling).
  • Quadrant II: STAT-only score above threshold and RIG-I-only score below threshold (bystander cells responding to secreted IFN).

Panels produced (all saved in figures/figure_03/):

Panel file Content
gathering_loske_dataset.pdf RIG-I-only vs STAT-only scores of all cells, split by SARS-CoV-2 status and coloured by quadrant
barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf Cell-type composition of quadrant I, quadrant II and all cells of SARS-CoV-2 positive donors, with the Fisher-test (BH-adjusted) p-value for enrichment of each cell type in quadrant I
scatterplot_rig_vs_stat_selected_cell_types.pdf RIG-I-only vs STAT-only scores of cells carrying SARS-CoV-2 transcripts in selected cell types, coloured by viral load
neutrophils_features_scov2pos.pdf RIG-I-only vs STAT-only scores of neutrophils carrying SARS-CoV-2 transcripts coloured by viral load, age group and IFNL1 expression

The code was taken from the original analysis script /media/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/interferon_model/scripts/R/july_2026/03_scRNASeq_projections_loske.Rmd (which wrote these panels to figures/2026_May/ on 2026-10-01), except for the cell-type barplot (barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf), which was produced on 2026-05-18 by an earlier version of /media/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/interferon_model/scripts/R/may_2026/03_scRNASeq_projections_loske.Rmd (see the section Cell-type composition of the quadrants for details). Only the code needed for these panels was kept; plotting code, PDF sizes and aesthetics are unchanged.

The neutrophil subset defined at the end of this markdown (SARS-CoV-2 transcript-positive neutrophils used for the children vs adults comparison) is saved to analysis/figure_03/ and is the input of supplementary_figure_03.Rmd (volcano plot and GSEA), so this markdown has to be run before supplementary_figure_03.Rmd.

Input data

Input Absolute path / source
Processed Seurat object of the nasal-swab scRNA-Seq data (raw counts, normalised data, UMAP and cell annotation as published by the authors; file 210716_figshare_upload_ag_lehmann.rds downloaded from the figshare repository of Loske et al. 2021 (see the Data availability section of the paper)). Viral transcripts are included as features SARS-CoV-2-p (positive strand) and SARS-CoV-2-m (minus strand) /media/bq-storage/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/data/loske_2021/210716_figshare_upload_ag_lehmann.rds
Cell metadata used (columns of the Seurat object above, as provided by Loske et al.) detailed_clusters (cell type), covid (SARS-CoV-2 status of the donor: pos / neg), covid_kid1 (status x age group: pos_adult, pos_children, neg_adult, neg_children), dps (days post symptom onset)
Viral load per cell SARS-CoV-2-p expression (normalised data of the Seurat object above)
RIG-I-only / STAT-only signatures (written by figure_01.Rmd) /media/bq-storage/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/decoupling_rigi_ifn/analysis/figure_01/rigi_vs_stat_only_signatures.rds (path2signs in settings.R)
Shared settings (paths, colours) /media/bq-storage/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/decoupling_rigi_ifn/scripts/R/settings.R

No MSigDB gene sets are used for the panels of this figure.

library(ggplot2)

library(gridExtra)

library(colorspace)

Loading signatures

RIG-I-only and STAT-only signatures defined in Figure 1. As in the original analysis, interferon genes (IFNB / IFNL) are removed from the signatures before scoring, and the list is reordered as (stat_only, rigi_only), so that AddModuleScore names the scores stat_only1 and rigi_only2.

signatures <- readRDS(path2signs)
signatures <- lapply(signatures,
                     function(genes){
                             genes[!grepl('IFNB|IFNL', genes)]
})
signatures <- signatures[c(2,1)]
str(signatures)
## List of 2
##  $ stat_only: chr [1:99] "PNPT1" "TRIM5" "CSF1" "ZNF711" ...
##  $ rigi_only: chr [1:94] "EGR4" "CXCL11" "FOSB" "EGR2" ...

Scoring cells

Module scores of both signatures for every cell (AddModuleScore uses a fixed seed by default, so scores are reproducible).

seurat <- AddModuleScore(seurat,
                         features = signatures,
                         name = names(signatures))
## Warning: The following features are not present in the object: HCP5, ANO7L1,
## AC009950.1, PSMB8-AS1, ADGRE1, SHFL, not searching for symbol synonyms
## Warning: The following features are not present in the object: CXCL8, NOCT,
## NEURL3, HIF1A-AS3, HSD17B7P2, ATP4A, RTL9, AC018398.1, AL606500.1, AC099489.1,
## AL353743.4, not searching for symbol synonyms
seurat@meta.data %>% colnames

Virtual gathering (panel gathering_loske_dataset.pdf)

Quadrant thresholds are computed from cells of SARS-CoV-2 negative donors (99.99 % quantile of stat_only1, 99.959 % quantile of rigi_only2). Quadrant I: stat_only1 <= stat_th & rigi_only2 >= rigi_th; quadrant II: stat_only1 >= stat_th & rigi_only2 <= rigi_th; all other cells are NA (grey). All cells are plotted, split by SARS-CoV-2 status of the donor.

md <- FetchData(seurat,
                vars = c(colnames(seurat@meta.data),
                         'SARS-CoV-2-p'))

cols <- brewer.pal(4, "Set2")[2:4]
names(cols) <- c("I", "II")

stat_th <- quantile(subset(md, covid == 'neg')$stat_only1, 0.9999)
stat_th
##    99.99% 
## 0.6079971
rigi_th <- quantile(subset(md, covid == 'neg')$rigi_only2, 0.99959)
rigi_th
##   99.959% 
## 0.5582593
md <-  md %>%
  mutate(
    quadrant = case_when(
      stat_only1 <= stat_th & rigi_only2 >= rigi_th ~ "I",
      stat_only1 >= stat_th & rigi_only2 <= rigi_th   ~ "II",
      FALSE ~ "III"
    )
  )
gathering_loske <- md %>%  ggplot(aes(x = rigi_only2, y = stat_only1, color = quadrant)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1, shape = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = stat_th, linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_vline(xintercept = rigi_th, linetype = 'dashed') +
  theme_bw() +
        facet_wrap(~covid) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(
    x = "rigi_only2",
    y = "stat_only1",
    color = "Quadrant"
  ) +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1.0))

gathering_loske

pdf(paste0(path2figures,
           '/gathering_loske_dataset.pdf'),
    width=5, height=2.75)
gathering_loske

Cell-type composition of the quadrants (panel barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf)

Provenance of this panel. The figure panel /media/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/interferon_model/figures/2026_May/barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf (2026-05-18) was produced by an earlier version of /media/ag-cherrmann/cramirez/interferon_model/scripts/R/may_2026/03_scRNASeq_projections_loske.Rmd. The current version of that script contains the same plotting code but labels the “Total” column with a string pasting the quadrant I and quadrant II FDRs from a separate test (results_joined, computed in a later chunk) and saves the plot as barplots_cell_types_fdr.pdf (2026-06-24). Comparing both PDFs, the bars and percentages are identical, but the qII panel shows labels of the form adj.p = 4e-54, i.e. the p_label column built in this very chunk from the BH-adjusted Fisher-test p-value of enrichment of each cell type in quadrant I (padj_I). Therefore, the code below is the current may_2026 code with the label of the p-value text layer set to p_label (data plot_df) instead of the FDR string of plot_df_fdr; everything else (bars, colours, sizes, the 7 x 3 inch PDF) is unchanged. The output is saved under the name of the figure panel, barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf.

Proportions are computed among cells of SARS-CoV-2 positive donors for all cells (“Total”), quadrant I and quadrant II, keeping the cell types present in quadrant I. For each cell type, a Fisher’s exact test compares the cell type vs all other cells in quadrant I vs outside quadrant I, and p-values are BH-adjusted.

# =========================================================
# 1. Compute proportions
# =========================================================

## Preparing the data
# keep only relevant columns
df <- md %>%
  filter(covid == "pos") %>%
  select(detailed_clusters, quadrant)

# total number of cells
n_total <- nrow(df)

prop_total <- df %>%
  count(detailed_clusters) %>%
  mutate(
    group = "Total",
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  )

prop_I <- df %>%
  filter(quadrant == "I") %>%
  count(detailed_clusters) %>%
  mutate(
    group = "I",
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  )

prop_II <- df %>%
  filter(quadrant == "II") %>%
  count(detailed_clusters) %>%
  mutate(
    group = "II",
    proportion = n / sum(n)
  )

props <- bind_rows(
  prop_total,
  prop_I,
  prop_II
)

# =========================================================
# 2. Keep only clusters present in quadrant I
# =========================================================


clusters_keep <- prop_I %>%
  filter(proportion > 0) %>%
  pull(detailed_clusters)

props <- props %>%
  filter(detailed_clusters %in% clusters_keep)

# =========================================================
# 3. Fisher enrichment tests
# =========================================================

df_test <- df

clusters <- unique(props$detailed_clusters)

enrichment_results <- lapply(clusters, function(cl){

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Fisher test for Quadrant I enrichment
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  tab_I <- matrix(c(

    # cluster in I
    sum(
      df_test$detailed_clusters == cl &
        df_test$quadrant == "I",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    # other clusters in I
    sum(
      df_test$detailed_clusters != cl &
        df_test$quadrant == "I",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    # cluster not in I
    sum(
      df_test$detailed_clusters == cl &
        df_test$quadrant != "I",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    # other clusters not in I
    sum(
      df_test$detailed_clusters != cl &
        df_test$quadrant != "I",
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

  ),
  nrow = 2,
  byrow = TRUE)

  test_I <- fisher.test(tab_I)

  data.frame(
    detailed_clusters = cl,
    p_I = test_I$p.value,
    OR_I = test_I$estimate
  )

}) %>%
  bind_rows()

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Adjust p-values
# ---------------------------------------------------------

enrichment_results <- enrichment_results %>%
  mutate(
    padj_I = p.adjust(p_I, method = "BH")
  )

# =========================================================
# 4. Merge
# =========================================================

plot_df <- props %>%
  left_join(
    enrichment_results,
    by = "detailed_clusters"
  )

# =========================================================
# 5. Labels
# =========================================================

plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(

    proportion_pct = round(
      proportion * 100,
      1
    ),

    prop_label = paste0(
      proportion_pct,
      "%"
    ),

    p_label = paste0(
      "adj.p = ",
      signif(padj_I, 2)
    )
  )

# =========================================================
# 6. Order clusters
# =========================================================

cluster_order <- prop_I %>%
  arrange(desc(proportion)) %>%
  pull(detailed_clusters)

plot_df$detailed_clusters <- factor(
  plot_df$detailed_clusters,
  levels = rev(cluster_order)
)

# =========================================================
# 7. TRUE 0-100% SCALE
# =========================================================
# Bars now represent actual percentages
# instead of scaling to group maxima
# =========================================================

plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(
    scaled_prop = proportion
  )

# =========================================================
# 8. Palette
# =========================================================

n_clusters <- length(
  unique(plot_df$detailed_clusters)
)

pal <- qualitative_hcl(
  n_clusters,
  palette = "Dark 3"
)

names(pal) <- levels(
  plot_df$detailed_clusters
)

# =========================================================
# 9. Plot
# =========================================================

barplots_cell_types <- ggplot(
  plot_df,
  aes(
    x = group,
    y = detailed_clusters
  )
) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # background boxes (100% width)
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = as.numeric(factor(group)) - 0.40,
      xmax = as.numeric(factor(group)) + 0.40,

      ymin = as.numeric(detailed_clusters) - 0.33,
      ymax = as.numeric(detailed_clusters) + 0.33
    ),
    fill = "white",
    color = "black",
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # loading bars
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_rect(
    aes(

      xmin = as.numeric(factor(group)) - 0.40,

      xmax =
        (as.numeric(factor(group)) - 0.40) +
        scaled_prop * 0.80,

      ymin = as.numeric(detailed_clusters) - 0.22,
      ymax = as.numeric(detailed_clusters) + 0.22,

      fill = detailed_clusters
    ),
    color = NA
  ) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # proportion labels
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_text(
    data = subset(plot_df, group == "I"),
    aes(label = prop_label),
    x = 0.58,
    size = 3,
    hjust = 1
  ) +

  geom_text(
    data = subset(plot_df, group == "II"),
    aes(label = prop_label),
    x = 1.58,
    size = 3,
    hjust = 1
  ) +

  geom_text(
    data = subset(plot_df, group == "Total"),
    aes(label = prop_label),
    x = 2.58,
    size = 3,
    hjust = 1
  ) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # p-value labels (quadrant I enrichment, BH-adjusted)
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_text(
    data = subset(plot_df, group == "Total"),
    aes(label = p_label),
    x = 3.08,
    size = 2.6,
    hjust = 0
  ) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # colors
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # theme
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),

    axis.title = element_blank(),

    legend.position = "none",

    axis.text.x = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 12
    ),

    axis.text.y = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),

    panel.background = element_rect(
      fill = "grey96",
      color = NA
    )
  )



pdf(paste0(path2figures,
           '/barplots_cell_types_qII.pdf'),
    width=7.0, height=3.0)
barplots_cell_types
dev.off()

Neutrophils of SARS-CoV-2 positive donors (panel neutrophils_features_scov2pos.pdf)

        dplyr::filter( ! covid_kid1 %in% c('neg_adult',
                                        'neg_children')) %>%
        dplyr::filter(detailed_clusters %in% c(
                                        'Neutrophil') ) %>%
 ggplot(aes(x = rigi_only2,
                          y = stat_only1,
                          colour = covid_kid1)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.0, linetype = 'dashed') +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 3)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12),
    strip.background = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "RIGI-only Score",
    y = "STAT-only Score",
    title = ""
  )

gridExtra::grid.arrange(neu_sarscov2,
                        neu_stage,
                        neu_ifnl, ncol = 3)

pdf(paste0(path2figures,

    height=4.0, width=14)
gridExtra::grid.arrange(neu_sarscov2,

Neutrophil subset for the children vs adults comparison (input of Supplementary Figure 3)

Same neutrophils as above, excluding children neutrophils with low RIG-I-only score (rigi_only2 < 0.5) and all neutrophils with stat_only1 >= 0.25, as in the original analysis. This subset is the input of the differential expression analysis (children vs adults) in supplementary_figure_03.Rmd, and is saved to analysis/figure_03/seurat_neutrophils_scov2pos_children_vs_adults.rds.

selected_cells <- df_signatures %>%
        dplyr::filter(`SARS-CoV-2-p` > 0 |
                              `SARS-CoV-2-m` > 0) %>%
        dplyr::filter( ! covid_kid1 %in% c('neg_adult',
                                        'neg_children')) %>%
        dplyr::filter(detailed_clusters %in% c(
                                        'Neutrophil') )  %>%
        dplyr::filter( ! ( rigi_only2 < 0.5 &
                                  covid_kid1 == 'pos_children' ) ) %>%
        rownames()


seurat_subset <- seurat[, selected_cells]
seurat_subset <- subset(seurat_subset, stat_only1 < 0.25)

seurat_subset$covid_kid1 %>% table
## .
## neg_children    neg_adult pos_children    pos_adult 
##            0            0           38           41
saveRDS(seurat_subset,
        file = paste0(path2analysis,
                      "/seurat_neutrophils_scov2pos_children_vs_adults.rds"))
